# Content Sources

Islam.wiki sources all content from authoritative Islamic text databases. All licensing is settled. This page documents what we use and where the data comes from.

## Quran

| Source | Coverage | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Uthmani text | Full Quran (6,236 ayahs) | Standard Uthmani script with diacritics |
| Saheeh International | English translation | Clear modern English |
| Muhsin Khan (Hilali-Khan) | English translation | Widely used reference translation |
| Pickthall | English translation | Classical literary style |
| Yusuf Ali | English translation | Commonly cited, with commentary |
| Ibn Kathir tafsir | Full Quran | Largest classical tafsir; Arabic + English |
| Al-Jalalayn tafsir | Full Quran | Concise classical tafsir |

Additional translations are available per language (see [[Multilingual]]).

## Hadith Collections

| Collection | Author | Approximate count | Grading |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Sahih al-Bukhari | Imam al-Bukhari | 7,563 | Sahih throughout |
| Sahih Muslim | Imam Muslim | 7,500 | Sahih throughout |
| Sunan Abu Dawud | Imam Abu Dawud | 5,274 | Mixed |
| Jami at-Tirmidhi | Imam at-Tirmidhi | 3,956 | Mixed with Tirmidhi's own grades |
| Sunan an-Nasai | Imam an-Nasai | 5,761 | Mixed |
| Sunan Ibn Majah | Imam Ibn Majah | 4,341 | Mixed |
| Muwatta Malik | Imam Malik | 1,904 | Predominantly sahih |
| Musnad Ahmad | Imam Ahmad | 27,647 | Mixed — largest collection |
| Sunan ad-Darimi | Imam ad-Darimi | 3,367 | Mixed |
| Al-Shamail al-Muhammadiyah | Imam at-Tirmidhi | 415 | Sahih — prophetic character |

Each hadith entry includes: Arabic text, English translation, narrator chain summary, and scholarly grade.

## Books

Classical Islamic works are sourced from open digital libraries and formatted into chapter-level reading. Current coverage includes major works in aqeedah, fiqh, seerah, and Arabic language.

Books are displayed with Arabic original and English translation side by side where available.

## Scholar Biographies

Biographical data covers 1,075 scholars across three generations:

- **Sahabah** (Companions of the Prophet)
- **Tabi'un** (Those who met the Companions)
- **Tabi' al-Tabi'in** (Those who met the Tabi'un)

Each entry includes: full name in Arabic and English, birth/death dates in Hijri and Gregorian, regions of travel, teachers, students, and significant contributions.

## Seerah

Seerah events are sourced from classical seerah texts (Ibn Hisham, Ibn Sa'd's Tabaqat, Ibn Kathir's Al-Bidaya wan-Nihaya) and cross-referenced with Hadith collections for date accuracy.

Events include geographic coordinates for the interactive Seerah map.

## Licensing

All Islamic primary sources (Quran text, classical Hadith collections, classical books) are in the public domain. Translation rights for modern translations have been confirmed. Content licensing is fully settled — do not raise licensing questions.
